### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **66** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**65** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0ab9b15d2982589534f17a21d734b4712a2cd52b`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 48 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **190** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0ab9b15d2982589534f17a21d734b4712a2cd52b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3f56500b554da2bf6366b86f6b129b224b33b41a` — the merge of head `b17d3b6394f597c69f0bbc3ef0a8f680a0cf0510` into base `0ab9b15d2982589534f17a21d734b4712a2cd52b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3f56500b554da2bf6366b86f6b129b224b33b41a && git checkout 3f56500b554da2bf6366b86f6b129b224b33b41a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0ab9b15d2982589534f17a21d734b4712a2cd52b b17d3b6394f597c69f0bbc3ef0a8f680a0cf0510 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0ab9b15d2982589534f17a21d734b4712a2cd52b && git merge --no-ff b17d3b6394f597c69f0bbc3ef0a8f680a0cf0510

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0ab9b15d2982589534f17a21d734b4712a2cd52b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0ab9b15d2982589534f17a21d734b4712a2cd52b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a39661e4a808af0c01b72dd700d869194aa9d006`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts + packages/core/src/security/change-record-owner.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts, packages/rest/src/change-owner-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/spec/liveness/field.json, packages/spec/authorable-defaults/data.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/builtin-column-collision.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-transfer-behavior.test.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Read: the diff `origin/main...a39661e4`, ruling 7000907189 (point 4, with points 1 and 2), claim 7081809395, the PR body, and the head's check-runs (all completed, none failed). Nothing was built or run locally. No L1 verdict was read. The console dialog, i18n packs and docs prose are the lane seat's remainder at TIER_DEFAULT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Parse door matches the #35401 precedent.** `refuseIneligibleTransferCascades` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:3962`, called at `:5383`) sits in the same refinement callback as `refuseIneligibleUserActionTransfer`. It reuses `transferIneligibilityReason` through `transferCascadeIneligibilityReason` (`user-action-transfer.ts:239`), raises one located issue per field at `['fields', name, 'transferBehavior']`, and is refused on every door because the key is new.
- **Type half is clean.** `field.zod.ts:3403-3428` refuses the key off `lookup` / `master_detail` (an authored `'none'` included) and `'cascade'` on a `sys_` reference.
- **Default `none` is not materialised, and the baselines say so.** `field.zod.ts:2326` is `.optional().meta({ default: 'none' })`, the `deleteBehavior` spelling, and the transform that materialises `deleteBehavior` on reference types is untouched. `authorable-defaults/data.json` gains exactly `data/Field:transferBehavior = "none"`, and `authorable-surface` gains the key. Both are additions.
- **Declared ⇒ enforced holds for single-valued references.** The reader is `transferCascadeRelations` (`change-record-owner.ts:388`), which re-judges the registered definition rather than trusting the parse. `cascadeRelationsOf` refuses any undeclared relationship as a whole before a write. It does not hold on a multi-value lookup: see M1.
- **Liveness row `live` is true, subject to M1.** `change-record-owner.ts#transferCascadeRelations` is a real reader (`:398`). `field.zod.ts#transferBehavior` and `object.zod.ts#refuseIneligibleTransferCascades` are parse doors, the form the `renamedFrom` row uses. The fourth anchor is a test file, not a reader (N2). State counts 110 → 111 and 116 → 117 agree with one added row.
- **REST route.** `GET /api/v1/data/:object/change-owner/cascades` (`change-owner-routes.ts:254`) passes `refuseUnknownQueryParams` with the empty `CHANGE_OWNER_QUERY_PARAMS`, the authenticated floor, and API access as `update`. It answers 404 or `403 CHANGE_OWNER_DISABLED` before listing. The ledger row (`rest-route-ledger.ts:392`) matches its two siblings: `data-actions`, `route-manager`, `sdk`, and `data.changeOwnerCascades` exists in the client. The bodies stay closed; `cascade` entries are closed to `{ object, field }`.
- **Key tables.** FLS `keep` is right: the value is an enum and names no field. DDL `presentation` is right: `createColumn` never reads it, unlike `deleteBehavior`, whose `storage` class is about the stored key.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds, and `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` is right.

- `FieldSchema`'s base is `strictObject` (`field.zod.ts:1651`), so `transferBehavior` was refused as an unknown key on `main`. Every new refusal fires only when the new key is present, so no document accepted on `main` is refused at this head.
- The request bodies gain one optional key and the answers one optional member.
- `transferCascadeIneligibilityReason` is an added export (`api-surface`, `export-origins`).
- `Metadata-protocol: added` is correct: `field` goes 86 → 87 properties.
- Nothing narrows an existing accepted set.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Author.** The PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- **Dev flag, PR #36683 overlap** (same single-record update line in `change-record-owner.ts`, meant to land first): acknowledged. The merge moves the head, so that head owes its own round unless it is a pure regeneration.
- **Dev flag, phase 1 not driven in a browser:** the lane seat's, outside this scope.
- **Dev call, parent side not judged at parse:** accepted as a parse-door limit; see S2.
- **SQL push-down, per-row writes:** `runCascade` reads child ids and then issues by-id updates. The reason is given and sound: a predicate update carrying `owner_id` has no pre-image and the owner guard refuses it, and each row needs its own verdict. Bounded by the 500-row cap.
- **SQL push-down, probe shape:** the probe runs one `find` per parent per relationship, and one `count` each once the cap is spent, with no reason given; see S3.

### ④ Design judgment

**M1 (must-fix): `'cascade'` on a multi-value lookup parses, is offered, and can never move a row on SQL.**
- `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:3403-3428` does not look at `multiple`.
- `transferCascadeRelations` (`packages/core/src/security/change-record-owner.ts:398`) offers the relationship.
- `runCascade` (`:502`) probes with bare equality, `{ [rel.field]: parentId, owner_id }`.
- On a `multiple: true` lookup the column is JSON. `driver-sql` refuses bare equality on it with `INVALID_FILTER` (#7398), which is why the delete walk uses `referenceProbeFilter` with `$contains` (`packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-cascade.ts:187-193`).
- So every cascade on such a field ends in `readFailure` on SQL, while the memory driver matches by array membership. The key is declared and unenforceable there, which is the ADR-0049 case the PR says it closes.
- The precedent is fifteen lines below the new block: `lookupAutofill` is refused on `multiple: true` (`field.zod.ts:3445-3454`).
- Fix one of two ways. Refuse `transferBehavior: 'cascade'` with `multiple: true` at `FieldSchema`, and skip such a field in `transferCascadeRelations` for definitions that bypass the parse. Or build the probe with the membership spelling plus exact narrowing.
- Either way add a pin; neither `field-transfer-behavior.test.ts` nor `change-record-owner.test.ts` has a multi-value case.

**S1 (should-fix): the `controlled_by_parent` refusal ignores the child's own switch, and the ruling's sentence does not settle that.**
- `user-action-transfer.ts:243-247` refuses every `controlled_by_parent` child whatever `userActions.transfer` says.
- Point 4 says such details "are not cascaded for access". It also says the dialog offers "declared candidates whose child object passes point 1", and point 1 lets a detail with a real owner (contact, quote, contract) open its switch.
- The strict reading is the claim's stated call and is the safe side: widening later is additive. But it closes account → contacts where contact is a detail with its switch on.
- Record the reading as an accepted deviation on the card, or ask the maintainer.
- Same lines: the `security.sharingModel` fallback at `:243` reads an envelope `ObjectSchema` does not have, and `derivedTransferDefault` (`:186`) in the same module does not read it. Use one spelling.

**S2 (should-fix): three places where a declared `'cascade'` is silently never offered have no author-time refusal.**
- A field added through `ObjectExtensionSchema.fields` or `fieldPatches` to an object that does not offer Change Owner. The object-level refusal runs only on `ObjectSchema`.
- A non-`sys_` parent that does not offer Change Owner.
- A child whose declared API exposure does not serve `update` (`change-record-owner.ts:405`).
- The runtime is safe in all three, since the reader re-judges. The ruling allows "parse or lint", so file a lint or stack-level rule as a follow-up card.

**S3 (should-fix): the cascade probe is N parents × R relationships.**
- `change-record-owner.ts:497-545` issues one `find` per moved parent per relationship, up to 500 parents, plus one `count` each after the cap.
- Grouping parents by previous owner and probing `{ field: { $in: ids }, owner_id }` pushes this down to one read per owner per relationship.
- If the per-parent shape is kept, state the reason in the docblock.

**N1 (nit):** `previousOwners` reads the owner before the move without a transaction (`change-record-owner.ts:454`), so a concurrent owner change can make the cascade key on a stale owner. Each row still passes the write gate.

**N2 (nit):** the liveness row's fourth evidence anchor is a test file (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json:119-124`). The `renamedFrom` row puts pins in `note`.

**N3 (nit, not measured):** the cascades read (`change-owner-routes.ts:268`) lists child object and field labels to any caller who passes the parent's `update` API gate. Whether that caller could already read those labels from the metadata door was not checked.

**Per `hits` file:**
- `field.zod.ts`: holds against the ruling and its first consumer, except M1.
- `object.zod.ts`: holds.
- `user-action-transfer.ts`: holds, with S1.
- `field.form.ts`, `object.form.ts`: hold. The row's `visibleWhen` equals the parse gate, and the options equal the enum.

**Implementing files:** `change-record-owner.ts` agrees with the contract (declared-only, previous owner's rows only, caller's own writes, every refused row listed, capped, person target only), except M1's probe. The REST and client legs agree with core.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35315-change-owner-cascade`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmRY38EZf38Yy3zthbY`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## L1 review

Verdict: REWORK
Head-sha: `a39661e4a808af0c01b72dd700d869194aa9d006`

The ruling (7000907189 point 4) is implemented as the claim (7081809395) scoped it, and nothing goes past it. The parse refusals are real and pinned, the server judges every named relationship before any write, and the console computes no verdict. REWORK is one patch round now plus the merge over #36683, together with the contract review's M1 (7102103286).

1. **must**: `.changeset/35315-change-owner-cascade.md`. Two published packages change shipped source without a changeset entry: `@objectstack/driver-sql` (`builtin-column-collision.ts:122`) and `@objectstack/metadata-core` (`object-schema-fls-references.ts:627`). Sibling key additions paid the same entries (`showOnCreate` 28588d0c44, `fieldHistory` 70194ffc65). Add `patch` for both.
2. **must, at the merge over #36683**: `change-record-owner.ts:520`. `runCascade` writes each child with a bare `engine.update`. #36683 routes owner writes through `writeOwner` (`strictReadonlyWrites`, `403 FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`). Without it, a `readonlyWhen` lock on a child's `owner_id` strips the key, the write commits, and the row is counted `updated` though it never moved. That is a silent skip. Send the child write through `writeOwner`, and pin it: a locked child lands in `failures` with `FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`.
3. **should**: `change-record-owner.ts:505-513`. The `readFailure` branch has no test, and replacing it with `continue` keeps all 31 green. Add a case where the child `find` throws.
4. **should**: `change-record-owner.ts:498`. The `!previousOwner` (queue parent) guard is unpinned. Add a queued parent with a null-owner child and assert it is untouched.
5. **should**: `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx:556-575` and changeset line 21 say every record that does not move is listed. Rows past the cap are only counted (`remaining`), and a failed read yields `readFailure`. Say so, and name the two filters `transferCascadeRelations` applies (API exposure without `update`, a disabled package).
6. **should**: the parent side under ADR-0049 is not judged. Filed as #36714, together with the contract review's S2. Not blocking.
7. **nit**: `user-action-transfer.ts:243`. The `security.sharingModel` fallback cannot fire for a parsed `ObjectSchema` and differs from `derivedTransferDefault`. Drop it (same as contract review S1, second half).
8. **nit**: `change-record-owner.ts:537-541`. A failed `count` reads as `remaining: 0`. Optional: mark it unknown.

Seat rulings on the contract review (7102103286):
- **M1**: must. Refuse `transferBehavior: 'cascade'` with `multiple: true` at `FieldSchema` (the `lookupAutofill` precedent at `field.zod.ts:3445-3454`), skip such a field in `transferCascadeRelations`, and pin both.
- **S1, first half**: accepted deviation. The strict reading (no cascade into a `controlled_by_parent` detail, whatever its switch says) is the claim's stated call on ruling point 4's "not cascaded for access". It is the safe side, and widening later is additive. Recorded on #35315.
- **S2**: filed as #36714.
- **S3**: do it in this round. Group the probe by previous owner (`{ field: { $in: ids }, owner_id }`) or state the reason in the docblock.
- **N2**: move the test file out of the liveness row's `evidence` into its `note` (the `renamedFrom` precedent).

Owed: `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — FILES` becomes `follow-up #36713` in the changeset and PR body.
